title: write()-before-ioctl for IKM is the right pattern for large/PQ key material
description: IKM is supplied via write() rather than embedded in struct crypto2dev_kdf_op. This is correct: ML-DSA-87 IKM could be 4896 bytes; embedding that in an ioctl struct would put it on the kernel stack on every call, violating the ~1KB stack frame guideline. The write()-then-ioctl pattern allocates exactly what's needed from the inbuf heap. A contributor might suggest 'just put a u8 ikm[4096] in the struct for simplicity' — this is wrong and sets a bad precedent for future PQ materials. Keep the pattern.
close_reason: Code verified correct. Design decisions implemented as described.
